desc:
A train is a row of cars described by a binary string s: s[i] = '1' means car i carries contraband, and '0' means it does not. You must remove all cars that carry contraband (cars without contraband may stay or go). Three kinds of actions are available:

  • remove the leftmost remaining car, in 1 minute;
  • remove the rightmost remaining car, in 1 minute;
  • remove any single remaining car, wherever it is, in 2 minutes.

Return the minimum number of minutes needed to get rid of every car that carries contraband.

For example, s = "1100101" needs 5 minutes (remove the first two cars from the left, then the last three cars from the right; the zeros in the middle may stay) and s = "0010" needs 2 minutes.
constraints: s contains only the characters '0' and '1'
hints: Whatever you do, the cars removed from the left end form a prefix and the cars removed from the right end form a suffix; the cars removed from the middle are the only ones that cost 2 each.
Split the train at a cut point i. Clear the part s[0:i] as cheaply as possible using left removals and middle removals, and clear s[i:] using right removals and middle removals. Then minimise over i.

Let left[i] be the best cost for the first i cars: left[i] = min(left[i-1] + (2 if s[i-1] == '1' else 0), i) (either handle the last car on its own, or remove all i from the left). Build right[i] symmetrically and take min(left[i] + right[i]).
editorial: Any plan removes some cars from the left end, some from the right end and some from the middle. The left-end removals are a prefix s[0:a], the right-end removals a suffix s[b:], and each flagged car between them costs 2. Unflagged cars in the middle can simply stay. So the plan costs a + (n - b) + 2 * (flagged cars in [a, b)).

Define left[i] as the cheapest way to clear the flagged cars of the prefix s[0:i] when only left-end and middle removals are available. Either strip the entire prefix from the left (cost i), or leave the last car i-1 to a middle removal (cost 2 if it is flagged, 0 otherwise) and solve the shorter prefix: left[i] = min(i, left[i-1] + (2 if s[i-1] == '1' else 0)). In the same way right[i] = min(n - i, right[i+1] + (2 if s[i] == '1' else 0)) for the suffix s[i:].

A cut at i splits the work between the two sides, so the answer is the minimum over i from 0 to n of left[i] + right[i]. For "1100101" the best cut leaves 5 minutes: clear the first two cars from the left (2 minutes) and the last three cars from the right (3 minutes); the zeros in the middle can stay. Time O(n), space O(n).
